topic: The Fundamental Bridge: The Relationship Between Integrals and Derivatives

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Velocity-Distance Analogy
lecture_lines: Derivatives represent the rate of change.
Integrals measure the accumulation of change.
A speedometer shows the current velocity.
Distance is the total area accumulated.
animations: Create a car element at left using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/car.png], color #FFFFFF.
Animate [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/car.png] moving right, creating a rectangular area beneath.

sections.title: Visualizing the Inverse Operation
lecture_lines: Derivatives find the slope of a curve.
Integrals find the area under a curve.
animations: Show graph of velocity [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speedometer.svg], horizontal line at y=v.
Highlight the area under the curve as integral.
Show the inverse movement: retrieving area from curve [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/calculator.svg].

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (Part 1)
lecture_lines: The Fundamental Theorem connects these two.
Integrating the rate gives net change.
It equals final position minus initial.
animations: Define area function A(x) = integral f(t)dt.
Show moving vertical line at x, color #FFFFFF [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/line.svg].
